cloud_review_note: All four distinct test groups, source retrieval and final retained-output audits ran in one workflow at the same source commit. Both9-test occurrences and fourOK results are checked explicitly; these are not independent observational experiments.
scientific_review: Three retained editorial current corridors are sampled at exact2022-01-15/07-15T00Z: Brazil eight vertices/sixteen cases/eighty velocity profiles; Benguela seven/fourteen/seventy;Canary nine/eighteen/ninety. Every original route vertex and five fixed normal offsets are preserved. These undated geographic sketches are not validated contemporary axes or physical current polygons.

Primary10cm/s is an exploratory OSW component diagnostic for the faster upper-ocean Brazil branch;primary5cm/s is used for the slower Benguela andCanary branches. All three retain5/10/20cm/s same-node sensitivity cases and qualifying cores in0–200m. These choices are not author-adopted unique physical boundaries or one universal definition for every current. Published inverse-density/transport interfaces are not equated to these component contours.

Source nearest-longitude selection uses circular angular distance with the first native index breaking ties. Brazil andCanary negative atlas longitudes correctly resolve source0–360grid coordinates. Native source longitude/global index and normalized[-180,180) sampled coordinates remain alongside each target/nearest-cell distance. Tests include wrong-hemisphere lookup, cyclic boundary/tie behavior and invalid axes. Oversized cyclic bounding slabs fail the field budget before retrieval.

At each original reference vertex, the neighboring-vertex WGS84 tangent defines a fixed component frame through depth. Five offsets(-40,-20,0,20,40km) sample nearest source nodes within8km. The frozen peak-core selector chooses the strongest qualifying downstream0–200m sample above the per-object primary threshold, with fixed first-offset tie order. No search expansion, axis forcing or independent alternate-node contour choice occurs.

The41 resolved primary lower crossings comprise Brazil11of16,Benguela12of14,Canary18of18. Twenty-six chosen maxima occur at an outermost offset(Brazil8,Benguela7,Canary11); three cases have no qualifying core(Brazil1,Benguela2). These edge and no-core flags stay unresolved for current-axis use. A resolved contour at an edge-selected model node is not validated physical current depth; a missing bounded-window core is not evidence of current absence.

Resolved selected paired threshold layers at5/10/20cm/s are Brazil9/11/14,Benguela12/11/8,Canary18/15/9. Alternate contours retain the primary-selected horizontal node and their own qualifying cores, both boundaries/native brackets and censoring statuses. Differences represent operator sensitivity, not depth confidence intervals, actual annual variation or interchangeable branch definitions.

All240 profiles retain eastward/northward and signed projected components at40native standard depths0–5000m, complete source indexing, exact timestamps, source analysis lead time when supplied, variable/global metadata and canonical decoded-profile hashes. Fixed-bearing projection preserves deep opposing flow. The frozen no-core helper poleward label is forward-relabelled downstream for equatorward branches, with the original status separately retained; numerical behavior is unchanged.

Connected upper/lower layers require contiguous source support from the qualifying core. Native surface0m is an upper boundary only when connected above-threshold support reaches it; missing/dry/domain edges remain censored. Neither the5000m product limit, source bathymetry nor an instrument or density-domain bound becomes a physical flow bottom. Layer span is a model threshold distance, not whole-current thickness.

The source run retrieved154720velocity-cell pairs and1237760decoded east/north array bytes, below20000pairs-per-patch,250000cumulative and7MBdecoded total caps. Coordinate axes were read first; each patch was checked before field reads. Source units, standard names, array dimensions, positive-down metre depths, instantaneous declaration, scaling and exact timestamps were verified. NetCDF-client wire bytes and source wire-byte SHA are not instrumented or claimed.

Thirty-eight checks include frozen contour, transport, paired-layer and Kuroshio behavior plus new cyclic-longitude handling, route ownership/order/counts, invalid or duplicate geometry, current-specific primary thresholds, signed counterflow and missing-level censoring, same-node alternates, fixed edge/tie behavior, query budgets and retained ownership/key rejection. Each completed current undergoes a cloud retained-output audit reproducing selection/layers, decoded hashes, native/wrapped coordinates, exact keys/times and physical eligibility.

Primary provider HYCOM documentation and primary publisher regional circulation prose for Canary(Kounta2018) and Brazil/Benguela(Cainzos2023) were freshly reviewed. They support source model/time definitions and broad branch geography, not the editorial intermediate coordinates, our threshold choices or physical current boundaries. No source figures were digitized or new prose depth values admitted.

All ocean-field retrieval, contour/layer calculations, tests and retained-output audits ran sequentially in cloud on one idle CPU. Local work prepared small metadata/code, verified proof/source hashes and retained exact cloud bytes. Source acquisition completed successfully; its extended duration was not used as a reason to restart it. Existing701 canonical scoped depth references,29 regional projection scenarios and102 eddy-size references remain preserved.

This collection adds source candidates, not yet canonical physical depth admissions or new reference projection objects. Current-identity/axis corroboration, gap-preserving along-route projections, compatible lateral geometry, whole-route physical thickness, volumes, state passage, annual envelopes and runtime/UI integration remain further work. No whole-programme completion is asserted.
